Fresh review of the current deterministic_trace claim and all supplied entries. The claim requires deterministic checked projection, retained dynamic parentage and dispositions, canonical sorting only for explicitly unordered siblings, and closed-set or extensible required/forbidden assertions without scheduler-order or raw Salsa-ID semantics.

The ordinary sage_host::trace association points at trace_sort_key; I inspected its complete current file, not only that preview. snapshot_trace calls build_dynamic_trace then recursively normalizes Unmapped keys to the operation name, normalizes descendants, and sorts only explicitly unordered child groups. query_operation removes parenthesized debug arguments and whitespace; semantic span/phase identities remain semantic strings. Full TraceNode serialization supplies the canonical key, retaining source, phase, operation, disposition, multiplicity and nested children. The captured protocol declarations establish these fields and the key/order enums. The second sorting pass happens after recursive key normalization, so earlier dynamic-trace sorting on raw debug payloads does not dictate final unordered ordering. Equal serialized subtrees are indistinguishable in the projection. Sequential siblings and roots are left in their original order; this mechanism intentionally does not globally sort the event stream or flatten it.

Parentage comes from stack push/pop and attach_trace_node attaching to the active parent. Query leaves follow the same attachment rule. Query exits and leaves map Executed, Validated, Reused and Cancelled one-for-one; spans retain Observed, external metadata is Executed, and unfinished spans remain Observed. Snapshot normalization never changes dispositions or reparents nodes. These observations establish the projection mechanism by source inspection, not a claim that producer instrumentation or all consumers have been behaviorally verified.

The complete associated test set consists of one explicit TODO function, sage_meta::todo::crates_sage_inspector_inspection_deterministic_trace. It contains no assertions. Its prerequisite is association and review of complete evidence for producer-authored sequential/unordered groups, cold/warm/edit traces, forbidden fallback assertions, retained raw failure payloads, and poll-scoped async spans protecting parentage. Accepting that explicit evidence-integration deferral leaves coverage TODO. In particular, closed-set/extensible required-and-forbidden matching and absence of scheduler/ID semantics in actual assertions remain to be established by that evidence; the projection helper alone cannot prove them. The empty TODO would detect neither accidental sequential sorting, lost nesting/dispositions, nor raw-ID dependence. No executable test coverage or end-to-end completeness is claimed, and there are no N/A entries.

I executed fresh review start with the current coordinator instructions and captured protocol declarations plus the decisions policy using review read. No behavioral tests were run; the coordinator owns central suite execution. No Rust or other source edits were made. This current assessment accepts the ordinary projection implementation together with the explicitly deferred test evidence; it does not promote the TODO to implemented coverage. No edits are requested under the policy allowing justified explicit deferrals.
